newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend fall, rebound seen Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend fall, rebound seen Wednesday.

text.p: Polish shares extended Monday's fall to 15,696.0 but analysts saw a rise on Wednesday as the market continued its general flat trend before the public offering of copper firm KGHM Polska Miedz.
"It seems we'll stay around 16,000 points at least until the end of the public offering of KGHM Polska Miedz, another two weeks," said Roman Sosnowski of WBK AIB Asset Management.

The 1.3-1.7-billion-zloty offering starts on June 30, the day the large Bank Handlowy starts trade on the main market. Analysts said recent news of Handlowy's heavy oversubscription augured well for KGHM now and for listed shares later.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 1.1 percent to 15,696.0 points and turnover fell 7.6 percent to 107.6 million zlotys ($33.2 million) on all three markets. Losers led gainers by 81 to 11 with 14 stocks flat.

Analysts said a central bank deputy head's Tuesday statement that Poland faced a gaping current account deficit and a Czech-style financial crisis in 1998 if it failed to balance next year's budget represented a longer-term threat.

"Poland's macroeconomic situation now seems very good but the current account deficit is very high, which could cause second-half (zloty) devaluation pressure and hurt (stocks)," said Tomasz Berent, an analyst at IB Austria Securities.
Later on Tuesday the prime minister said he believed the bank had instruments to keep the current account deficit down.
Analysts said National Investment Funds (NFIs), down 5.3 percent to 139.4 points, were continuing to fall as ever more investors exchanged their NFI units for fund shares.

NFI units fell five percent on Tuesday to 141.5 zlotys ($43.7) but analysts said lower turnovers of the funds and units and strong buying after price fixing of the funds signalled a possible rebound on Wednesday.
